fullPassage:
[1번] One day, my father took me and my brother on a camping trip. While driving to a nearby forest, he explained how to set up the tent. Almost immediately after we arrived, however, my brother was stung by a wasp, which caused his forehead to swell. We tried to catch our dinner by fishing in a nearby lake, but we failed miserably, returning with nothing but dozens of mosquito bites. Without any fish, we cooked a can of beans over a campfire, which was an unwise endeavor that burned the bottom layer of beans while leaving those on top cold. When bedtime came, we unrolled my father's old sleeping bags to find them stinking of damp mold. The odor was so overpowering that even my father gave up. We packed the tent, got in the car, and drove home.

[2번] The Venus flytrap, a meat-eating plant, has a pair of leaves that act as jaws and a stomach. If an insect touches the trigger hairs on the surface of these leaves, the leaves close, trapping the insect. Amazingly, a recent experiment showed that the Venus flytrap knew how many times its trigger hairs were touched and could even count the time between these stimuli. The trap closed only if the plant sensed two stimuli within a 20 second time span. Once 20 seconds passed, the process was reset. In addition, more than three stimuli were required for the plant to begin producing the enzymes that digest the trapped insect. Thanks to this process, the Venus flytrap doesn't make meaningless efforts trying to trap and digest raindrops or fallen leaves.

[3번] The "Rat Park" was an experiment conducted by a psychologist in the late 1970s. It was used to show that a social community can be more powerful than drugs. In the experiment, rats were given a choice between two bottles, one containing plain water and the other containing water with morphine added to it. The psychologist found that rats kept together drank much less of the morphine water than rats kept alone. He concluded that addictive qualities aren't the only thing that promotes drug use. The social and environmental conditions of the individual also play an important role. This seems to apply to humans as well as rats. People who are lonely and isolated are more likely to become addicted to drugs. But if these conditions are improved, their chances of breaking the addiction increase. This means that social recovery could someday become a treatment for drug addiction.

[4번] "Negative pressure" refers to a situation in which the pressure of an enclosed area is lower than that of the surrounding area. If the barrier between these two areas breaks, any substances in the high-pressure area will immediately flow into the low-pressure area. For example, undersea pipes used to transport oil are in a state of negative pressure; therefore, any break in the pipeline will cause it to fill with ocean water. This is much better than the opposite scenario, in which oil would be released into the ocean. However, negative pressure is not always beneficial, such as in the case of pipes carrying drinking water to a city. If these municipal waterlines are damaged, they can potentially suck in contaminated groundwater, which would then enter the water supply. For this reason, a system of gauges and valves is used to adjust and control their pressure.

[5번] If astronauts travel to Mars in the near future, the journey will probably take years. Therefore, providing the astronauts with enough to eat will be a major challenge. Scientists are now looking for ways to allow astronauts to extend their food supply by growing crops. Seeds take up less storage space than packaged meals, and astronauts can plant them once they reach Mars. NASA is already conducting experiments to find out what might grow on Mars. The soil on Mars is made up mostly of crushed rocks, so it has few or no nutrients. In a test, NASA planted lettuce in crushed volcanic rock from Hawaii, which also contains few nutrients. The lettuce took a long time to grow, but it tasted normal. Because this test was a success, NASA now plans to find out how long other vegetables would take to grow on Mars.

[6번] Every four years, a twenty-ninth day is added to the month of February. This day, also known as Leap Day, was created to ensure that our calendar and our seasons stay in line with each other. While we think that a normal year consists of 365 days, it actually takes Earth about 365.2421 days to orbit the sun. Every four years, it is necessary to add an extra day to account for the lost time. Without the addition of a leap day, winter would occur earlier in the calendar year, causing problems for agricultural schedules and potentially leading to crop failures. Additionally, many holidays and cultural celebrations are linked to specific seasons or dates. Without leap years to keep the calendar in check, these events would gradually drift away from their intended time of celebration.

[7번] The urgency instinct is what allows people to act quickly when faced with danger. It is particularly useful in emergency situations, where making quick decisions is essential. However, in non-emergency situations, it can cause people to panic and make poor decisions. One example of the urgency instinct in mass media is the fear of terrorism. People in the Western world fear terrorism more than heart disease, despite the fact that heart disease represents a much greater threat. The reason for this is the media's coverage of terrorist attacks, which greatly exaggerates the threat of terrorism. In reality, the possibility of being killed in a terrorist attack is extremely low. The chances of dying from heart disease, on the other hand, are much higher. The urgency instinct causes us to feel that immediate action is required to combat terrorism, even though there are many more significant threats. This is why rational analysis is required. It allows us to counteract the urgency instinct and respond to risks accordingly.

[8번] In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, found a penguin struggling on the beach. The helpless, starving creature covered in oil was adopted by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim. Mr. de Souza nursed him back to health and released him, thinking they would never meet again. Amazingly, though, Dindim returned! It is believed that he traveled around 5,000 miles between Mr. de Souza's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile. What is more, he makes this journey every year. After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his annual migration for his breeding routine, only to return once again.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) driving=운전하며 / walking=걸으며 (B) cooked=요리했다 / ate=먹었다 (C) packed=(짐을) 쌌다 / unpacked=(짐을) 풀었다
det.analysis:
(A) 숲으로 '운전하며' 텐트 치는 법을 설명 → driving(차로 이동 중이므로 walking=걸으며는 부적절)
(B) 콩 통조림을 불에 '요리했다' → cooked(ate=먹었다는 앞뒤 안 맞음)
(C) 집에 가려고 텐트를 '쌌다' → packed(unpacked=풀었다는 반대, 집에 가는 상황)
원문 조합인 ③이 정답 ←정답
det.tip: 마지막에 집으로 돌아가려면 텐트를 packed(쌌다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 trapped와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: trapped=갇힌 / caught=잡힌 / freed=풀려난 / cooked=요리된 / hidden=숨겨진
det.analysis:
① caught: 잡힌 — trapped의 동의어
② freed: 풀려난 — trapped(갇힌)의 반의어 ←정답

questions.passage:
(A) Undersea oil pipes exist in a <u>state</u> of negative pressure, which keeps ocean water out unless a break suddenly occurs in the line.

questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 state의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: state: (A) 상태 (B) 주(州), 지역
det.analysis:
① (A) 상태 (B) 주: a state of negative pressure=음압 '상태', economy of his state=그의 '주(州)'의 경제 ←정답
② 순서가 뒤바뀜 — 부적절
③ (B) 진술하다: 주지사가 자신의 '주'를 언급, 진술하다가 아님
④ (A) 진술하다: 음압을 '진술하다'? 부적절
det.tip: state 다의어: 상태(a state of) vs 주(州)/지역(his state)

det.analysis:
① powerful—less—important: 사회적 공동체가 약물보다 강력하고, 함께 있던 쥐가 모르핀 물을 덜 마셨으며, 개인의 조건이 중요한 역할을 한다 ←정답
② weak: 약하다는 실험 결론(공동체가 더 강력)과 반대
③ more/trivial: 함께 있던 쥐는 더 적게 마셨고, 조건은 중요한 역할을 하므로 반대
④ weak/more: 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: Rat Park 실험의 핵심: 공동체가 약물보다 powerful, 함께 있으면 less 섭취, 환경 조건이 important

questions.passage: "Negative pressure" refers to a situation in which the pressure of an enclosed area is (A)[lower / higher] than that of the surrounding area. If the barrier between these two areas breaks, any substances in the high-pressure area will (B)[immediately / slowly] flow into the low-pressure area. For example, undersea pipes used to transport oil are in a state of negative pressure; therefore, any break in the pipeline will cause it to fill with ocean water. This is much (C)[worse / better] than the opposite scenario, in which oil would be released into the ocean. However, negative pressure is not always beneficial, such as in the case of pipes carrying drinking water to a city. If these municipal waterlines are damaged, they can potentially suck in contaminated groundwater, which would then enter the water supply. For this reason, a system of gauges and valves is used to adjust and control their pressure.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) lower=더 낮은 / higher=더 높은 (B) immediately=즉시 / slowly=천천히 (C) better=더 나은 / worse=더 나쁜
det.analysis:
① higher — immediately — worse: (A) 음압은 압력이 '더 낮은(lower)' 상태 — higher는 반대
② lower — slowly — better: (B) 장벽이 깨지면 '즉시(immediately)' 흐름 — slowly는 반대
③ lower — immediately — better: 음압=압력이 더 낮음, 장벽 붕괴 시 즉시 유입, 기름 유출보다 바닷물 유입이 더 나음(better) ←정답
④ higher — slowly — worse: 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 음압 정의(lower)+장벽 붕괴 시 즉각 유입(immediately)+기름 유출보다 나음(better)

questions.passage: If astronauts travel to Mars in the near future, the ①<u>journey</u> will probably take years. Therefore, providing the astronauts with enough to eat will be a major challenge. Scientists are now looking for ways to allow astronauts to ②<u>reduce</u> their food supply by growing crops. Seeds take up less storage space than packaged meals, and astronauts can plant them once they reach Mars. NASA is already ③<u>conducting</u> experiments to find out what might grow on Mars. The soil on Mars is made up mostly of crushed rocks, so it has few or no nutrients. In a test, NASA planted lettuce in crushed volcanic rock from Hawaii, which also contains few nutrients. The lettuce took a long time to grow, but it tasted normal. Because this test was a success, NASA now plans to find out how long other ④<u>vegetables</u> would take to grow on Mars.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① journey=여정 ② extend→reduce (부적절) ③ conducting=수행하는 ④ vegetables=채소
det.analysis:
① journey: 화성으로의 '여정'은 수년이 걸림 — 적절
② reduce: 작물을 길러 식량 공급을 '줄인다'? 늘리는 것이므로 extend가 원문 ←정답
③ conducting: NASA가 실험을 '수행하는' — 적절
④ vegetables: 다른 '채소'가 얼마나 걸릴지 — 적절
det.tip: 작물을 기르면 식량을 extend(늘림). reduce(줄임)는 반대

questions.passage: When bedtime came, we unrolled my father's old sleeping bags to find them __________ (stink) of damp mold. The odor was so overpowering that even my father gave up.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: stink(동사: 악취가 나다) → stinking(현재분사). find + 목적어 + -ing 구문
det.analysis: 'find them __________ of damp mold'에서 목적어(them) 뒤에 목적격보어로 현재분사가 필요해요. 'find + 목적어 + V-ing'는 '~가 …하고 있는 것을 발견하다'라는 뜻이라, stink를 stinking(악취를 풍기는)으로 바꿔 써요.
det.tip: find + 목적어 + V-ing = ~가 …하고 있는 것을 알게 되다 → stinking

questions.passage: Amazingly, a recent experiment showed that the Venus flytrap knew how many times its trigger hairs were __________ (touch).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: touch(동사: 건드리다) → touched(과거분사: 건드려진). were + p.p. 수동태 구문
det.analysis: touch를 과거분사 touched로 변환. 'its trigger hairs were touched'=감각모가 건드려졌다 — were + p.p. 수동태에서 과거분사가 필요
det.tip: were _____ → 수동태(be + p.p.) → touched

questions.passage: In the experiment, rats were __________ (give) a choice between two bottles, one containing plain water and the other containing water with morphine added to it. The psychologist found that rats kept together drank much less of the morphine water than rats kept alone.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: give(주다) → given(과거분사). were given = 수동태 '주어졌다'
det.analysis: give를 과거분사 given으로 변환. 'rats were given a choice' = '쥐들에게 선택권이 주어졌다' — be + p.p. 수동태 구문에서 과거분사 필요
det.tip: rats were ___ a choice → 수동태(be + p.p.) → given

questions.passage: "Negative pressure" refers to a situation in which the pressure of an __________ (enclose) area is lower than that of the surrounding area.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: enclose(동사: 둘러싸다) → enclosed(과거분사: 밀폐된). 명사 area를 수식하는 과거분사
det.analysis: enclose를 과거분사 enclosed로 변환. 'an enclosed area'=밀폐된 공간. 명사(area)를 앞에서 수식하며 '둘러싸인/밀폐된' 수동 의미를 나타내므로 과거분사가 필요
det.tip: 명사를 수식하며 '~된' 수동 의미 → 과거분사(enclosed)

questions.passage: NASA is already __________ (conduct) experiments to find out what might grow on Mars.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: conduct(수행하다) → conducting. 'is already ___'는 be동사 뒤이므로 현재진행형(be + V-ing)이 필요
det.analysis: conduct를 현재진행형 conducting으로 변환. 'NASA is already conducting' = 'NASA는 이미 실험을 수행하고 있다' — be동사(is) 뒤 진행형이므로 동사원형에 -ing
det.tip: be동사(is) + 이미(already) → 진행 중 → conduct + ing = conducting
